body:
Gold is trading firmly in record territory, with spot bouncing in the roughly $4,270–$4,350 per ounce range this week.

Gold price was trading at $4,277 per ounce as of 8:50 a.m. Eastern Time on September 14, a $112 increase from three days earlier and a $614 increase from a year ago. That trajectory shows up cleanly in the option-style markets: Kalshi's September 30 above $4,250.99 settlement contract sits almost exactly at a coin-flip (52¢ bid / 57¢ ask), which is what you'd expect when the strike sits near the middle of the market's expected distribution for spot at expiry. The broader move has been attributed to Fed easing and safe-haven flows — gold safe-haven demand has emerged as a catalyst driven by escalating geopolitical uncertainty, alongside softer monetary policy from three consecutive Fed rate cuts making investors more bullish.

The scanner flagged one item today, and it's not worth chasing. It pairs a Polymarket YES, gold's low touches $3,900 in September at 3.6¢ with NO, low touches $3,800 at 96.3¢, for a combined cost of 99.9¢ against a guaranteed $1 payout. The edge is a tenth of a cent per contract, capped at 243 contracts for a grand total of $0.24 in capturable profit — essentially rounding noise on two deep out-of-the-money, thinly traded strikes (spot is more than $400 above both thresholds), not a real mispricing.

No cross-platform arbitrage showed up between Kalshi and Polymarket gold contracts, and that's the normal state of things: Kalshi's contracts settle on the spot price at a fixed future moment, while Polymarket's touch contracts pay out if gold crosses a level anytime during the window. Those are different bets on different rules, so their prices aren't directly comparable even when the strikes look similar. Overall, a quiet day for arbitrage, layered on top of a genuinely newsworthy gold rally.
headline: Gold holds near record highs; scanner finds no real arbitrage, just rounding noise
